title: Add Timeframe Selector to Trade Entry Checker with Timeframe-Adapted Indicators

requirements.text: Add a 'Timeframe' selector to the Trade Entry Checker form with options: 1m, 15m, and 1h. Default the selection to 1m (the user's most-used timeframe). Display the selector prominently near the top of the form, before the indicator inputs.

quotes: beim checker wird nicht gefragt, um welchen Zeitrahmen es sich handelt. Bitte füge 1m, 15m und 1h hinzu. Wobei ich am meisten den 1m Rahmen benutze.

acceptanceCriteria: The Trade Entry Checker form includes a 'Timeframe' selector with exactly three options: 1m, 15m, 1h.
The default selected timeframe is 1m.
The selected timeframe is visually highlighted (e.g., button group or segmented control).
Changing the timeframe updates the form's indicator labels and hints without clearing already-entered values.

requirements.text: When the selected timeframe is 1m, replace the EMA20/EMA50/EMA200 inputs with EMA9 and EMA21 inputs (as these are the relevant fast EMAs for 1-minute charts). Hide the EMA200 field for 1m. Show EMA20, EMA50, EMA200 for 15m and 1h timeframes. Update all field labels accordingly.

quotes: Und passe die Indikatoren entsprechend an.

acceptanceCriteria: For timeframe=1m: the form shows EMA9 and EMA21 fields only (no EMA50, no EMA200).
For timeframe=15m and 1h: the form shows EMA20, EMA50, and EMA200 fields.
Field labels clearly reflect the EMA period (e.g., 'EMA9', 'EMA21', 'EMA20', etc.).
Switching timeframes updates the visible EMA fields immediately.

requirements.text: For the 1m timeframe, remove the MACD Direction input from the Trade Entry Checker form, as MACD is not recommended for 1-minute charts (too slow, too noisy). Display a short informational note explaining this omission (e.g., 'MACD is not recommended for 1m charts due to excessive noise.'). For 15m and 1h, keep the MACD Direction dropdown.

quotes: Und passe die Indikatoren entsprechend an.

acceptanceCriteria: For timeframe=1m: the MACD Direction dropdown is hidden and replaced with an informational note in English.
For timeframe=15m and 1h: the MACD Direction dropdown is shown as before.
The informational note is short and in English.

requirements.text: Adapt the ATR interpretation hint shown in the Trade Entry Checker form based on the selected timeframe. For 1m: show a note that ATR on 1m is only useful as an activity filter (not for SL/TP calculation) and is optional. For 15m and 1h: keep the standard ATR description. The ATR input field should be marked as optional for 1m and required for 15m/1h.

quotes: Und passe die Indikatoren entsprechend an.

acceptanceCriteria: For timeframe=1m: ATR field is labeled as optional and displays a note: 'On 1m charts, ATR is only useful as a market activity indicator, not for SL/TP. Leave blank if not available.'
For timeframe=15m and 1h: ATR is required and the standard description is shown.
Validation does not block submission on 1m if ATR is left blank.

requirements.text: Update the rule engine in tradeEntryRules.ts (or equivalent) to evaluate conditions based on the selected timeframe. For 1m: evaluate (1) EMA9 > EMA21 alignment (Long) or EMA9 < EMA21 (Short); (2) Price proximity: current price within 1× ATR of EMA9 (if ATR provided), else skip the proximity check; (3) RSI extremes use tighter thresholds: RSI < 75 for Long (not overbought), RSI > 25 for Short (not oversold). MACD condition is omitted for 1m. For 15m: use EMA20/EMA50/EMA200 alignment, RSI thresholds < 65 / > 35, and MACD as before. For 1h: same as 15m.

quotes: Und passe die Indikatoren entsprechend an.

acceptanceCriteria: For timeframe=1m: rule engine evaluates EMA9/EMA21 alignment, optional ATR proximity to EMA9, and RSI < 75 (Long) / RSI > 25 (Short). MACD is not evaluated.
For timeframe=15m and 1h: rule engine evaluates EMA20 > EMA50 > EMA200 alignment (Long), price within 1× ATR of EMA20, RSI < 65 (Long) / RSI > 35 (Short), and MACD direction.
The checklist in EntryChecklistResults reflects only the applicable conditions for the selected timeframe.
Failed condition explanations reference the correct EMA periods and RSI thresholds for the timeframe.

requirements.text: Display the selected timeframe in the Trade Entry Checker results summary card (alongside the asset name and trade direction badge), so the user always sees which timeframe the verdict was calculated for.

quotes: beim checker wird nicht gefragt, um welchen Zeitrahmen es sich handelt.

acceptanceCriteria: The summary verdict card in EntryChecklistResults shows the timeframe (e.g., '1m', '15m', '1h') as a label or badge.
The timeframe label is always visible when results are displayed.

constraints: Do not modify files listed in frontend.immutablePaths.
All user-facing text (labels, notes, error messages) must be in English.
Do not change the existing 15m/1h rule logic — only add 1m as a new mode alongside them.
The Reset button must clear the timeframe selector back to the default (1m).
nonGoals: Fetching real-time indicator values automatically — all inputs remain manual.
Backend changes — this is a purely frontend feature.
Changing the Orderbook Heatmap or any other tab.
